# Model and source

* Citation: Song IH, Chen G, Hayes S, Farrell C, Jomphe C, Gosselin NH, Sun K.
  Population pharmacokinetics and exposure-response relationships of maribavir
  in transplant recipients with cytomegalovirus infection. *J Pharmacokinet
  Pharmacodyn.* 2024;51:887-904.
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-024-09939-2>
* Online Supplementary Material 1 (the final NONMEM control stream, Tables
  S1.1-S1.3 and Figures S1.1-S1.5) is distributed with the article.

Song 2024 has two halves. The **population PK model** pools phase 1, phase 2 and
the phase 3 SOLSTICE study; its final model is the NONMEM run headed
`$PROB RUN# 171`, the same run already packaged as
`modellib("Sun_2023_maribavir")`. Every structural parameter, covariate effect
and residual variance in Song 2024 Table 2 reproduces that file to within
rounding (largest difference 0.26%, on Vc/F), and the control stream in the Song
2024 supplement has the same structure, so no second copy of the PK model is
packaged; this vignette uses `Sun_2023_maribavir` wherever a PK model
is needed.

The **exposure-response** half is new. It reports six logistic regressions
fitted to the 231-patient maribavir arm of SOLSTICE (transplant recipients with
CMV infection refractory to ganciclovir, valganciclovir, foscarnet or
cidofovir). Each was fitted independently, so each is its own model file:

```{r er-inventory}
er_models <- c(
  "Song_2024_maribavir_cmv_clearance_wk8",
  "Song_2024_maribavir_cmv_clearance_wk16",
  "Song_2024_maribavir_te_resistance",
  "Song_2024_maribavir_sae",
  "Song_2024_maribavir_dysgeusia",
  "Song_2024_maribavir_fatigue"
)
er_ui <- lapply(er_models, function(nm) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(nm)))
names(er_ui) <- er_models

er_ini <- function(nm) {
  d <- er_ui[[nm]]$iniDf
  stats::setNames(d$est, d$name)
}

inventory <- data.frame(
  Model = sub("^Song_2024_maribavir_", "", er_models),
  Endpoint = c(
    "Confirmed CMV DNA clearance at week 8 (primary)",
    "Clearance + symptom control at week 8, maintained to week 16 (key secondary)",
    "Treatment-emergent maribavir-resistant CMV mutation",
    "Treatment-emergent serious adverse event",
    "Taste disturbance (dysgeusia)",
    "Fatigue"
  ),
  `Exposure metric` = c("AUCss (0-24 h)", "AUCss (0-24 h)", "Ctrough,ss",
                        "AUCss (0-24 h)", "Cavg", "Cmax,ss"),
  Source = c("Table 5", "Table S1.3", "Table 6",
             "Figure S1.5 (digitised)", "Figure S1.3 (digitised)",
             "Figure S1.4 (digitised)"),
  `Risk factors` = vapply(er_models, function(nm) {
    sum(grepl("^e_", names(er_ini(nm)))) - 1L
  }, integer(1)),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(inventory, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "The six Song 2024 exposure-response models.")
```

All six are static landmark regressions: no ODE, no PK layer, no random
effects. The exposure enters as a data column, as it did in the source analysis,
where it was an individual (empirical-Bayes) prediction from the PK model on the
last day of maribavir exposure. The *End to end* section below derives those
columns from `Sun_2023_maribavir`.

Four exposure columns are used, and they are not interchangeable:

* `AUC_MBV_SS24` -- AUC from 0 to 24 h at steady state on the last day of
  exposure. Song 2024 calls this `AUCss`; it is a **full-day** integral (both
  doses of the twice-daily regimen), so it is twice the dosing-interval
  `AUC0-tau` of Song 2024 Table 3 and twice the `AUC_MBV_SS` used by the Sun
  2025 AURORA models. Tables 5 and S1.3 estimate the slope per 50 ug\*h/mL.
* `CTROUGH` -- trough at steady state on the last day, slope per 2.5 ug/mL.
* `CMAX` -- Cmax at steady state on the last day, slope per ug/mL.
* `CAV` -- average concentration, slope per ug/mL.

# Population

The exposure-response set is 231 of the 235 maribavir-arm SOLSTICE patients who
had PK exposure parameters (Song 2024 Table 4 and Table S1.2): age 19-79 years
(median 56), weight 36.1-124 kg (median 74.1), 62% male, 76% White, 13% Black,
4% Asian. 140 (61%) were solid organ and 91 (39%) haematopoietic cell transplant
recipients. Baseline CMV DNA was low (< 9100 IU/mL) in 151, intermediate in 66
and high (>= 91 000 IU/mL) in 14 -- cut-points from the SOLSTICE primary
publication (Avery 2022, *Clin Infect Dis*), whose maribavir-arm counts
(153 / 68 / 14 of 235) match. 100 patients carried CMV resistant to a prior
anti-CMV drug at baseline, 98 had received CMV prophylaxis, and 60 developed a
treatment-emergent maribavir-resistance mutation (47 during treatment, 13
after it). The CMV-specific CD4+CD69+ and CD8+CD69+ T-cell assays were
unreported for the same 46 patients.

The same information is in each model's `population` metadata:

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Song_2024_maribavir_te_resistance"))$population)
```

# Source trace

Every coefficient in the three printed-table models was transcribed from the
paper's `Estimate (SE)` column. The paper also prints an odds ratio for every
non-intercept row and defines it as the exponentiated estimate, which gives a
free check on the transcription: because both columns are rounded, the test is
whether **any** estimate inside the printed estimate's rounding interval
exponentiates into the printed odds ratio's rounding interval.

```{r source-trace}
printed <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model,                    ~parameter,                   ~estimate, ~or,       ~location,
  "cmv_clearance_wk8",       "logit_ref",                  "1.58",    NA,        "Table 5, Intercept",
  "cmv_clearance_wk8",       "e_auc_logit",                "-0.131",  "0.877",   "Table 5, AUCss per 50 ug*h/mL",
  "cmv_clearance_wk8",       "e_te_resist_mbv_ontx_logit", "-5.39",   "0.00457", "Table 5, TE resistance on treatment",
  "cmv_clearance_wk8",       "e_cd8_pp65_mid_logit",       "-0.304",  "0.739",   "Table 5, CD8+CD69+ >=0.5 to <2%",
  "cmv_clearance_wk8",       "e_cd8_pp65_hi_logit",        "1.19",    "3.29",    "Table 5, CD8+CD69+ >=2%",
  "cmv_clearance_wk8",       "e_cd8_pp65_nr_logit",        "-0.314",  "0.730",   "Table 5, CD8+CD69+ not reported",
  "cmv_clearance_wk16",      "logit_ref",                  "0.814",   NA,        "Table S1.3, Intercept",
  "cmv_clearance_wk16",      "e_auc_logit",                "-0.301",  "0.740",   "Table S1.3, AUCss per 50 ug*h/mL",
  "cmv_clearance_wk16",      "e_te_resist_mbv_logit",      "-3.27",   "0.0381",  "Table S1.3, TE resistance (any time)",
  "cmv_clearance_wk16",      "e_cd8_pp65_mid_logit",       "-0.521",  "0.594",   "Table S1.3, CD8+CD69+ >=0.5 to <2%",
  "cmv_clearance_wk16",      "e_cd8_pp65_hi_logit",        "1.65",    "5.18",    "Table S1.3, CD8+CD69+ >=2%",
  "cmv_clearance_wk16",      "e_cd8_pp65_nr_logit",        "-0.107",  "0.899",   "Table S1.3, CD8+CD69+ not reported",
  "cmv_clearance_wk16",      "e_cmvdna_high_logit",        "-1.01",   "0.363",   "Table S1.3, CMV DNA intermediate/high",
  "cmv_clearance_wk16",      "e_cmv_prophy_prior_logit",   "-0.818",  "0.441",   "Table S1.3, prior CMV prophylaxis",
  "te_resistance",           "logit_ref",                  "-0.242",  NA,        "Table 6, Intercept",
  "te_resistance",           "e_ctrough_logit",            "0.210",   "1.23",    "Table 6, Ctrough,ss per 2.5 ug/mL",
  "te_resistance",           "e_cmvdna_int_logit",         "0.694",   "2.00",    "Table 6, CMV DNA intermediate",
  "te_resistance",           "e_cmvdna_vhigh_logit",       "1.52",    "4.57",    "Table 6, CMV DNA high",
  "te_resistance",           "e_dis_cmv_res_bl_logit",     "-1.08",   "0.341",   "Table 6, CMV resistant at baseline",
  "te_resistance",           "e_cd4_pp65_mid_logit",       "-1.52",   "0.219",   "Table 6, CD4+CD69+ >=0.5 to <2%",
  "te_resistance",           "e_cd4_pp65_hi_logit",        "-0.0534", "0.948",   "Table 6, CD4+CD69+ >=2%",
  "te_resistance",           "e_cd4_pp65_nr_logit",        "-0.185",  "0.831",   "Table 6, CD4+CD69+ not reported",
  "te_resistance",           "e_age_logit",                "-0.0328", "0.968",   "Table 6, Age (per year)",
  "te_resistance",           "e_sot_logit",                "0.970",   "2.64",    "Table 6, Solid organ transplant"
)

# Half a unit in the last printed decimal place (estimate) or significant
# figure (odds ratio), i.e. the rounding interval the source's own numbers
# imply.
half_ulp_dec <- function(s) {
  d <- ifelse(grepl("\\.", s), nchar(sub("^[^.]*\\.", "", s)), 0)
  0.5 * 10^(-d)
}
half_ulp_sig <- function(s) {
  x <- as.numeric(s)
  digits <- nchar(gsub("^0+", "", gsub("[-.]", "", s)))
  0.5 * 10^(floor(log10(abs(x))) - digits + 1)
}

trace <- printed |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    packaged = unname(er_ini(paste0("Song_2024_maribavir_", model))[parameter]),
    matches_table = isTRUE(all.equal(packaged, as.numeric(estimate))),
    or_consistent = if (is.na(or)) NA else {
      h <- half_ulp_dec(estimate)
      u <- half_ulp_sig(or)
      b <- as.numeric(estimate)
      exp(b + h) >= as.numeric(or) - u && exp(b - h) <= as.numeric(or) + u
    }
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

knitr::kable(
  dplyr::select(trace, Model = model, Parameter = parameter,
                `Printed estimate` = estimate, `Printed OR` = or,
                `Packaged value` = packaged, `Matches` = matches_table,
                `OR consistent` = or_consistent, Location = location),
  caption = "Every printed-table coefficient against the packaged ini() value and against its own printed odds ratio."
)

or_bad <- trace[!is.na(trace$or_consistent) & !trace$or_consistent, ]
stopifnot(
  all(trace$matches_table),
  # One printed odds ratio disagrees with its own estimate: Table 5 prints
  # OR 0.739 for -0.304, but exp(-0.304) = 0.738 and no estimate that rounds
  # to -0.304 reaches 0.739. See Source discrepancies. Every other row agrees.
  nrow(or_bad) == 1L,
  or_bad$model == "cmv_clearance_wk8",
  or_bad$parameter == "e_cd8_pp65_mid_logit",
  # Every non-intercept ini() parameter of the three table models is traced.
  setequal(
    unlist(lapply(er_models[1:3], function(nm) {
      p <- names(er_ini(nm))
      paste(sub("^Song_2024_maribavir_", "", nm), p[!grepl("^addSd", p)])
    })),
    paste(trace$model, trace$parameter)
  )
)
```

The three safety models are a different kind of source. Song 2024 reports them
only as fitted curves in Supplementary Figures S1.3-S1.5, each with its p-value
and an observed-proportion quartile table, but with no coefficient table
anywhere. The maintainers digitised each curve: the axes were calibrated from
the labelled ticks, the fitted line was tracked column by column across the
figure raster (1338-1346 points per curve), and `logit(p)` was regressed on the
untransformed exposure.

| Model | Intercept | Slope | Logit-linear R^2 | Max \|residual\| (logit) | Curve x-range vs printed range |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sae (Figure S1.5, AUCss) | -1.467 | 0.003481 per ug\*h/mL | 0.999993 | 0.014 | 71.5-802.9 vs 72.2-802 |
| dysgeusia (Figure S1.3, Cavg) | 0.8056 | -0.07977 per ug/mL | 0.999990 | 0.012 | 3.48-38.4 vs 3.50-38.3 |
| fatigue (Figure S1.4, Cmax,ss) | -3.713 | 0.08244 per ug/mL | 0.999952 | 0.11 | 7.39-47.0 vs 7.37-47.0 |

A curve drawn from a linear-logit model is exactly linear on the logit scale,
so the near-unit R^2 confirms both the digitisation and that the exposure
enters untransformed. The recovered x-range of each curve reproduces the
separately printed exposure range, which the calibration did not use. The
*Mean-probability identity* section below adds an independent check against the
printed event counts.

| Equation element | Source |
|---|---|
| `logit(p) = alpha + beta * X` (linear exposure on the logit) | Methods, Exposure-response analysis of efficacy, first logistic equation |
| `logit(p) = alpha + beta1 * X1 + ... + betan * Xn` (additive covariates) | Methods, second logistic equation |
| Exposure metrics and their definitions | Abbreviations; Methods, Individual predicted PK parameters |
| Per-50 / per-2.5 increments | Table 5, Table 6, Table S1.3 row labels |
| Reference subjects | Table 5, Table 6, Table S1.3 footnotes |
| CMV DNA cut-points | Avery 2022 (SOLSTICE primary), Methods and Table 1 |

## The paper's own scenario probabilities

The Results text quotes predicted probabilities for named patient profiles.
They are reproduced below by solving the packaged model files, not by
re-deriving the algebra by hand.

```{r scenarios}
solve_one <- function(nm, covs) {
  ui <- er_ui[[nm]]
  ev <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, dv = NA_real_)
  for (cv in ui$allCovs) ev[[cv]] <- 0
  for (cv in names(covs)) ev[[cv]] <- covs[[cv]]
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui), ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  out[[grep("^prob_", names(out), value = TRUE)[1]]]
}

wk8  <- "Song_2024_maribavir_cmv_clearance_wk8"
wk16 <- "Song_2024_maribavir_cmv_clearance_wk16"
res  <- "Song_2024_maribavir_te_resistance"

# Table 5 / S1.3 scenarios are at AUCss 200 ug*h/mL. Table 6 scenarios are at
# Ctrough,ss 5 ug/mL in an HCT recipient (TX_HCT = 1), with the age term at
# zero -- the paper's "of the same age" phrasing; see Assumptions.
hct <- list(CTROUGH = 5, TX_HCT = 1)
scen <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Model,  ~Scenario,                         ~covs,                                                   ~Published,
  wk8,     "Reference",                       list(AUC_MBV_SS24 = 200),                                0.742,
  wk8,     "TE resistance on treatment",      list(AUC_MBV_SS24 = 200, TE_RESIST_MBV_ONTX = 1),         0.013,
  wk8,     "CD8+CD69+ >= 2%",                 list(AUC_MBV_SS24 = 200, CD8_PP65_HI = 1),                0.900,
  wk16,    "Reference",                       list(AUC_MBV_SS24 = 200),                                0.403,
  wk16,    "TE resistance (any time)",        list(AUC_MBV_SS24 = 200, TE_RESIST_MBV = 1),              0.025,
  wk16,    "CD8+CD69+ >= 2%",                 list(AUC_MBV_SS24 = 200, CD8_PP65_HI = 1),                0.779,
  wk16,    "CMV DNA intermediate/high",       list(AUC_MBV_SS24 = 200, CMVDNA_HIGH = 1),                0.197,
  wk16,    "Prior CMV prophylaxis",           list(AUC_MBV_SS24 = 200, CMV_PROPHY_PRIOR = 1),           0.230,
  res,     "Reference (HCT, low CMV DNA)",    hct,                                                     0.545,
  res,     "CMV DNA intermediate",            c(hct, CMVDNA_HIGH = 1),                                 0.705,
  res,     "CMV DNA high",                    c(hct, CMVDNA_HIGH = 1, CMVDNA_VHIGH = 1),               0.845,
  res,     "CMV resistant at baseline",       c(hct, DIS_CMV_RES_BL = 1),                              0.289,
  res,     "CD4+CD69+ >= 0.5 to < 2%",        c(hct, CD4_PP65_MID = 1),                                0.207,
  res,     "Solid organ transplant",          list(CTROUGH = 5, TX_HCT = 0),                           0.759
)
scen$Predicted <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(scen)), function(i) {
  solve_one(scen$Model[i], scen$covs[[i]])
}, numeric(1))

scen_tab <- scen |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Model = sub("^Song_2024_maribavir_", "", Model),
    Predicted = round(Predicted, 4),
    Difference = round(Predicted - Published, 4)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(Model, Scenario, Published, Predicted, Difference)
knitr::kable(scen_tab, caption = "Results-text scenario probabilities against the packaged models.")

big <- abs(scen_tab$Difference) >= 0.0025
stopifnot(
  # Thirteen of the fourteen reproduce to the printed precision (the quoted
  # percentage's own rounding plus the coefficients' rounding).
  sum(big) == 1L,
  # The exception is the Table 5 CD8+CD69+ >= 2% profile, quoted as 90.0%.
  # The packaged coefficients give 0.904, and no choice of coefficients inside
  # their printed rounding intervals reaches 0.900 (the lowest is 0.903); see
  # Assumptions and deviations.
  scen_tab$Scenario[big] == "CD8+CD69+ >= 2%",
  scen_tab$Model[big] == "cmv_clearance_wk8",
  abs(scen_tab$Difference[big]) < 0.006
)
```

# Virtual cohort

The packaged models need exposures, and the paper's exposures came from the PK
model. This section simulates a SOLSTICE-like cohort of 200 transplant
recipients with CMV through `Sun_2023_maribavir` at 400 mg twice daily, then
attaches baseline risk factors drawn from the published Table 4 / Table S1.2
proportions.

Weights are log-normal, matched to the Table 4 mean 75.7 kg and SD 17.9 kg, and
redrawn (not clamped) until they fall inside the reported 36.1-124 kg range.
Ages are normal, matched to mean 53.7 and SD 13.4, redrawn into 19-79 years.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20240927)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240927)

n_sub <- 200L

draw_bounded <- function(n, rdraw, lo, hi) {
  x <- rdraw(n)
  repeat {
    bad <- x < lo | x > hi
    if (!any(bad)) return(x)
    x[bad] <- rdraw(sum(bad))
  }
}
wt_sdlog <- sqrt(log1p((17.9 / 75.7)^2))
wt_meanlog <- log(75.7) - wt_sdlog^2 / 2

cohort <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = draw_bounded(n_sub, function(n) stats::rlnorm(n, wt_meanlog, wt_sdlog), 36.1, 124),
  AGE = draw_bounded(n_sub, function(n) stats::rnorm(n, 53.7, 13.4), 19, 79),
  TX_HCT = stats::rbinom(n_sub, 1, 91 / 231),
  cmvdna = sample(c("low", "int", "high"), n_sub, TRUE, prob = c(151, 66, 14)),
  DIS_CMV_RES_BL = stats::rbinom(n_sub, 1, 100 / 231),
  CMV_PROPHY_PRIOR = stats::rbinom(n_sub, 1, 98 / 231),
  # The CD4 and CD8 assays were unreported for the same 46 patients.
  assay_nr = stats::rbinom(n_sub, 1, 46 / 231),
  cd4 = sample(c("lo", "mid", "hi"), n_sub, TRUE, prob = c(131, 42, 12)),
  cd8 = sample(c("lo", "mid", "hi"), n_sub, TRUE, prob = c(128, 28, 29)),
  # Treatment-emergent resistance: 60 of 231 at any time, 47 of those 60
  # during treatment.
  TE_RESIST_MBV = stats::rbinom(n_sub, 1, 60 / 231)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    TE_RESIST_MBV_ONTX = TE_RESIST_MBV * stats::rbinom(dplyr::n(), 1, 47 / 60),
    CMVDNA_HIGH  = as.integer(cmvdna != "low"),
    CMVDNA_VHIGH = as.integer(cmvdna == "high"),
    CD4_PP65_MID = as.integer(assay_nr == 0 & cd4 == "mid"),
    CD4_PP65_HI  = as.integer(assay_nr == 0 & cd4 == "hi"),
    CD4_PP65_NR  = assay_nr,
    CD8_PP65_MID = as.integer(assay_nr == 0 & cd8 == "mid"),
    CD8_PP65_HI  = as.integer(assay_nr == 0 & cd8 == "hi"),
    CD8_PP65_NR  = assay_nr
  )

cohort |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Weight median (kg)` = round(stats::median(WT), 1),
    `Age median (y)` = round(stats::median(AGE), 1),
    `HCT %` = round(100 * mean(TX_HCT), 1),
    `CMV DNA >= 9100 %` = round(100 * mean(CMVDNA_HIGH), 1),
    `CD8/CD4 not reported %` = round(100 * mean(assay_nr), 1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated cohort (targets: weight median 74.1 kg, age median 56, HCT 39%, CMV DNA >= 9100 IU/mL 35%, assay not reported 20%).")
```

# Simulation

400 mg twice daily for 10 days (20 doses), far beyond the 2 days to steady
state. The observation grid covers the last full day, 216-240 h, so that both
the 24 h `AUCss` of the exposure-response models and the dosing-interval
`AUC0-tau` of Table 3 come from the same steady-state profiles. No concomitant
CYP3A inhibitor or inducer is given.

```{r simulate}
mod_pk <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sun_2023_maribavir"))

ev_pk <- rxode2::et(amt = 400, ii = 12, addl = 19, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(216, 240, by = 0.1), cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(id = cohort$id) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(cohort, id, WT), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    DOSE = 400, DIS_CMV = 1,
    CONMED_CYP3A4_INH = 0, CONMED_CYP3A4_IND = 0
  )

sim_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk, ev_pk, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "400 mg BID")
```

```{r fig-profiles, fig.cap = "Simulated steady-state maribavir profiles over the last day of 400 mg twice daily in transplant recipients with CMV (median and 5th-95th percentiles)."}
sim_pk |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    med = stats::median(Cc),
    lo = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    hi = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(time - 216, med)) +
  ggplot2::geom_ribbon(ggplot2::aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Time in the last day of dosing (h)",
                y = "Maribavir concentration (ug/mL)")
```

# PKNCA validation

Two intervals per subject: the last 12 h dosing interval (228-240 h) for the
Table 3 comparison, and the whole last day (216-240 h) for the 24 h `AUCss` the
exposure-response models consume.

```{r pknca}
conc_data <- sim_pk |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, Cc)

dose_data <- tibble::tibble(
  id = rep(cohort$id, each = 2),
  treatment = "400 mg BID",
  time = rep(c(216, 228), times = n_sub),
  dose = 400
)

o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_data, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_data, dose ~ time | treatment + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(228, 216), end = c(240, 240),
  auclast = TRUE, cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE), cmin = c(TRUE, FALSE)
)

o_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))
nca_res <- as.data.frame(o_nca)

stopifnot(nrow(nca_res) > 0L, !anyNA(nca_res$PPORRES))

nca_tau <- dplyr::filter(nca_res, start == 228)
nca_day <- dplyr::filter(nca_res, start == 216, PPTESTCD == "auclast")
```

# Comparison against published NCA

Song 2024 Table 3 reports geometric mean (CV%) steady-state exposure at 400 mg
twice daily for the 253 SOLSTICE refractory patients with PK, from post-hoc
individual estimates: `AUC0-tau` 129 ug\*h/mL (51.6%), `Cmax,ss` 16.9 ug/mL
(39.1%), `Ctrough,ss` 5.13 ug/mL (93.0%).

```{r nca-comparison}
reference <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,    ~PPTESTCD, ~PPORRES,
  "400 mg BID",  "auclast",   129,
  "400 mg BID",  "cmax",       16.9,
  "400 mg BID",  "cmin",        5.13
)

nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_tau,
  reference = reference,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c(
    "AUC0-tau (ug*h/mL)" = "auclast",
    "Cmax,ss (ug/mL)" = "cmax",
    "Ctrough,ss (ug/mL)" = "cmin"
  ),
  label_first_column = "NCA parameter"
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated versus Song 2024 Table 3 (SOLSTICE refractory) steady-state exposure. Values marked with a star differ by more than 20%.")

gm_check <- nca_tau |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax", "cmin")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    gm = exp(mean(log(PPORRES))),
    cv = 100 * sqrt(exp(stats::var(log(PPORRES))) - 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(reference, by = "PPTESTCD") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (gm - PPORRES) / PPORRES)

gm_check |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  dplyr::select(PPTESTCD, simulated_gm = gm, simulated_cv = cv,
                published_gm = PPORRES, pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Geometric means, the statistic Table 3 reports.")

stopifnot(
  # AUC and Cmax are set by CL/F and Vc/F, the best-determined parameters; a
  # mis-transcribed PK model moves them by tens of percent.
  max(abs(gm_check$pct_diff[gm_check$PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax")])) < 15,
  # The trough is absorption- and lag-driven and the most variable metric.
  abs(gm_check$pct_diff[gm_check$PPTESTCD == "cmin"]) < 30
)

# The 24 h AUC is the sum of two identical steady-state intervals.
day_ratio <- stats::median(
  nca_day$PPORRES /
    nca_tau$PPORRES[nca_tau$PPTESTCD == "auclast"][match(nca_day$id, nca_tau$id[nca_tau$PPTESTCD == "auclast"])]
)
day_ratio
stopifnot(abs(day_ratio - 2) < 0.01)
```

All three simulated geometric means sit within about 12% of Table 3 and on the
high side. Two differences in the comparison are expected to contribute: the
simulated cohort carries no concomitant medication, whereas Table 3 includes
patients on strong CYP3A inhibitors or inducers, and Table 3 summarises
post-hoc estimates that are shrunk toward the typical value rather than
prospective draws from the full IIV. The gates above allow 15% for AUC and Cmax
and 30% for the much more variable trough.

The ratio check is the one that matters for the exposure-response models: the
24 h `AUCss` they consume is exactly twice the dosing-interval AUC. Song 2024's
own numbers agree -- Table 3's `AUC0-tau` geometric mean of 129 ug\*h/mL is
consistent with the median `AUCss` of about 238 ug\*h/mL printed in Figure S1.5.

# Exposure-response: end to end

The simulated exposures and risk factors are now fed through all six models.

```{r er-cohort}
expo <- nca_tau |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::rename(CMAX = cmax, CTROUGH = cmin) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::transmute(nca_day, id, AUC_MBV_SS24 = PPORRES),
    by = "id"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(CAV = AUC_MBV_SS24 / 24)

er_data <- dplyr::left_join(cohort, expo, by = "id")

predict_er <- function(nm, data) {
  ui <- er_ui[[nm]]
  ev <- data.frame(id = data$id, time = 0, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, dv = NA_real_)
  for (cv in ui$allCovs) ev[[cv]] <- data[[cv]]
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui), ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  out[[grep("^prob_", names(out), value = TRUE)[1]]]
}

er_pred <- lapply(er_models, predict_er, data = er_data)
names(er_pred) <- er_models

stopifnot(all(vapply(er_pred, function(p) all(p > 0 & p < 1), logical(1))))

expo |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(c(AUC_MBV_SS24, CTROUGH, CMAX, CAV),
                                 \(x) round(stats::median(x), 2))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median simulated exposure columns (Figure S1.5 median AUCss about 238 ug*h/mL; Figure S1.3 median Cavg about 10.6 ug/mL; Figure S1.4 median Cmax,ss about 17.6 ug/mL).")
```

The simulated medians run above the figure medians, in line with the Table 3
comparison above; the exposure-response analysis set is also not identical to
the 253-patient Table 3 set.

## Mean-probability identity

For a logistic regression fitted by maximum likelihood with an intercept, the
mean fitted probability over the analysis set equals the observed event rate.
The simulated cohort is not the analysis set -- its covariates are drawn
independently from published marginals, and its exposures are prospective
rather than post-hoc -- so the identity holds only approximately. It is still a
sharp check on the coefficient scale: a slope off by a factor of 50, an exposure
column off by a factor of 2, or an uncentred term that should have been centred
moves the mean probability by far more than these approximations do. For the
digitised safety models it is a check made with numbers the digitisation never
used.

```{r identity}
identity <- tibble::tibble(
  Model = sub("^Song_2024_maribavir_", "", er_models),
  Observed = c(131, 44, 60, 88, 108, 28) / 231,
  `Mean predicted` = vapply(er_pred, mean, numeric(1))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Difference = `Mean predicted` - Observed)

knitr::kable(identity, digits = 3,
             caption = "Mean predicted probability over the simulated cohort against the observed event rate in the 231-patient analysis set.")

stopifnot(max(abs(identity$Difference)) < 0.06)
```

Two encoding choices rest on this identity. Table 6 enters age **uncentred**:
with an age term centred at the median of 56 years, the mean predicted
probability of resistance would be about 0.6 against an observed 0.26. And the
efficacy models need the **24 h** AUC: supplying the 12 h `AUC0-tau` instead
would lift the predicted week-16 response rate well above the observed 19%.

```{r identity-alternatives}
p_age_centred <- mean(stats::plogis(
  qlogis(er_pred[[res]]) - er_ini(res)[["e_age_logit"]] * 56
))
p_auc_tau <- mean(predict_er(wk16, dplyr::mutate(er_data, AUC_MBV_SS24 = AUC_MBV_SS24 / 2)))
c(age_centred_resistance = p_age_centred, wk16_with_auc_tau = p_auc_tau)
stopifnot(
  abs(p_age_centred - 60 / 231) > 0.2,
  p_auc_tau - 44 / 231 > 0.05
)
```

## Exposure-response curves

```{r fig-efficacy, fig.cap = "Primary (Table 5) and key secondary (Table S1.3) endpoints against the 0-24 h steady-state AUC for the reference patient (no resistance mutation, CD8+CD69+ < 0.5%, low CMV DNA, no prior prophylaxis), with the effect of a treatment-emergent resistance mutation. Song 2024 Figure 4 and Figure S1.2 show the exposure-only fits for the same endpoints; the curves here are the final multivariable models."}
auc_grid <- seq(72, 802, length.out = 100)
curve_eff <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c(wk8, wk16), function(nm) {
  te_col <- if (nm == wk8) "TE_RESIST_MBV_ONTX" else "TE_RESIST_MBV"
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(0:1, function(te) {
    d <- data.frame(id = seq_along(auc_grid), AUC_MBV_SS24 = auc_grid)
    for (cv in setdiff(er_ui[[nm]]$allCovs, "AUC_MBV_SS24")) d[[cv]] <- 0
    d[[te_col]] <- te
    data.frame(
      endpoint = if (nm == wk8) "Week 8 (primary)" else "Week 16 maintained (key secondary)",
      resistance = if (te == 1) "TE resistance mutation" else "No TE resistance",
      AUC = auc_grid, p = predict_er(nm, d)
    )
  }))
}))
ggplot2::ggplot(curve_eff, ggplot2::aes(AUC, p, linetype = resistance)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~endpoint) +
  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "AUCss, 0-24 h (ug*h/mL)", y = "Probability of response", linetype = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r fig-resistance, fig.cap = "Probability of a treatment-emergent maribavir-resistant mutation (Table 6) against steady-state trough concentration, by baseline CMV DNA, for a 56-year-old HCT recipient without baseline resistance and CD4+CD69+ < 0.5%. Compare with Song 2024 Figure 5, which shows the exposure-only fit."}
ct_grid <- seq(0.5, 20, length.out = 100)
curve_res <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("low", "int", "high"), function(lvl) {
  d <- data.frame(id = seq_along(ct_grid), CTROUGH = ct_grid)
  for (cv in setdiff(er_ui[[res]]$allCovs, "CTROUGH")) d[[cv]] <- 0
  d$AGE <- 56
  d$TX_HCT <- 1
  d$CMVDNA_HIGH <- as.integer(lvl != "low")
  d$CMVDNA_VHIGH <- as.integer(lvl == "high")
  data.frame(cmvdna = lvl, Ctrough = ct_grid, p = predict_er(res, d))
}))
curve_res$cmvdna <- factor(curve_res$cmvdna, c("low", "int", "high"),
                           c("Low (< 9100 IU/mL)", "Intermediate", "High (>= 91 000 IU/mL)"))
ggplot2::ggplot(curve_res, ggplot2::aes(Ctrough, p, colour = cmvdna)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Ctrough,ss (ug/mL)", y = "Probability of TE resistance",
                colour = "Baseline CMV DNA") +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r fig-safety, fig.cap = "Replicates Song 2024 Figures S1.3-S1.5: the packaged safety models (lines) against the observed event proportions and 95% CIs in each exposure quartile, as printed beneath each figure (points at the quartile mid-range)."}
quart <- tibble::tribble(
  ~endpoint,       ~lo,  ~hi,   ~obs,  ~lcl,  ~ucl,
  "sae",           72.2, 170,   0.293, 0.181, 0.427,
  "sae",           170,  238,   0.351, 0.229, 0.489,
  "sae",           238,  354,   0.345, 0.225, 0.481,
  "sae",           354,  802,   0.534, 0.399, 0.667,
  "dysgeusia",     3.50, 7.83,  0.534, 0.399, 0.667,
  "dysgeusia",     7.83, 10.6,  0.579, 0.441, 0.709,
  "dysgeusia",     10.6, 14.6,  0.448, 0.317, 0.585,
  "dysgeusia",     14.6, 38.3,  0.310, 0.195, 0.445,
  "fatigue",       7.37, 12.9,  0.052, 0.011, 0.144,
  "fatigue",       12.9, 17.6,  0.088, 0.029, 0.193,
  "fatigue",       17.6, 22.6,  0.086, 0.029, 0.190,
  "fatigue",       22.6, 47.0,  0.259, 0.153, 0.390
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(x = (lo + hi) / 2)

saf <- c(sae = "AUC_MBV_SS24", dysgeusia = "CAV", fatigue = "CMAX")
curve_saf <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(saf), function(ep) {
  rng <- range(quart$lo[quart$endpoint == ep], quart$hi[quart$endpoint == ep])
  x <- seq(rng[1], rng[2], length.out = 100)

  d[[saf[[ep]]]] <- x

}))
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_line(data = curve_saf, ggplot2::aes(x, p)) +
  ggplot2::geom_pointrange(data = quart, ggplot2::aes(x, obs, ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl)) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~endpoint, scales = "free_x",
                      labeller = ggplot2::labeller(endpoint = c(
                        sae = "Serious AE vs AUCss (ug*h/mL)",
                        dysgeusia = "Taste disturbance vs Cavg (ug/mL)",
                        fatigue = "Fatigue vs Cmax,ss (ug/mL)"))) +
  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Probability")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

## The PK model is not repackaged

Song 2024's final popPK model is the NONMEM run already packaged as
`Sun_2023_maribavir`, and its Table 2 reproduces that file to within rounding.
The Song 2024 supplement prints only the *initial* `$THETA` / `$OMEGA` estimates
of that run, so the existing file -- whose source carried the converged values
and the full OMEGA block -- is the better-sourced copy.

## The three safety models are digitised, univariate fits

* **Coefficients recovered from figures.** Song 2024 prints no coefficient table
  for the taste-disturbance, fatigue and serious-adverse-event models, only the
  fitted curves in Supplementary Figures S1.3-S1.5 with their p-values. The
  intercepts and slopes were digitised by the maintainers as described in the
  Source trace, and are rounded to four significant figures. Treat them as
  reproductions of the plotted curves, not as published estimates.
* **They are the exposure-only fits.** The paper's final safety models also
  retained other risk factors -- transplant type and enrolment region for taste
  disturbance, enrolment region for fatigue, baseline CMV resistance and
  baseline CMV DNA for serious adverse events -- whose coefficients are not
  reported. The figures draw the exposure-only regression, and that is what is
  packaged. The unreported terms are recorded in each file's
  `covariatesDataExcluded` or covariate notes.
* **Cavg is per patient.** Song 2024 defines Cavg as the "average concentration
  on each study day" and plots one value per patient, without saying how the
  days were summarised. At steady state the daily average is `AUCss / 24`,
  which is what this vignette supplies.

## Covariate encoding

* **Two nested CMV DNA indicators.** `CMVDNA_HIGH` marks `>= 9100 IU/mL` and
  `CMVDNA_VHIGH` marks `>= 91 000 IU/mL`, so Table 6's three levels are
  `CMVDNA_HIGH - CMVDNA_VHIGH` (intermediate) and `CMVDNA_VHIGH` (high), and
  Table S1.3's pooled "intermediate/high" is `CMVDNA_HIGH`. Song 2024 does not
  print the cut-points; they come from the SOLSTICE primary publication (Avery
  2022). Note that the Sun 2025 AURORA paper calls `>= 9100 IU/mL` "high": the
  same word names different cut-points in the two trials.
* **Two nested resistance indicators.** The primary-endpoint model uses a
  mutation detected *during* treatment (`TE_RESIST_MBV_ONTX`, 47 patients), the
  key-secondary model a mutation detected *at any time* (`TE_RESIST_MBV`, 60).
  Both are on-study outcomes used as predictors of another on-study outcome, so
  these coefficients describe association, not baseline prognosis.
* **Solid organ transplant as `1 - TX_HCT`.** Exact for this cohort of 140 SOT
  and 91 HCT recipients with no non-transplant subject.
* **Not reported is a fitted level.** `CD8_PP65_NR` / `CD4_PP65_NR` carry their
  own coefficients. A result reported as "too few cells for analysis" is not
  "not reported": Table S1.2 footnote a assigns it to the `< 0.5%` reference.
* **Baseline CMV resistance, 5 unreported.** The paper does not say how the 5
  patients with unreported baseline resistance were coded.

## Source discrepancies

* **One printed odds ratio disagrees with its estimate.** Table 5 prints
  `-0.304` with odds ratio `0.739` for the CD8+CD69+ `>= 0.5% to < 2%` stratum,
  but `exp(-0.304) = 0.738`, and no estimate that rounds to `-0.304` gives an
  odds ratio that rounds to `0.739`. The other twenty printed odds ratios agree
  with their estimates. The packaged value is the printed estimate; the
  difference is far below the coefficient's standard error (0.492).
* **One Results-text probability does not reproduce.** The Table 5 profile with
  CD8+CD69+ `>= 2%` is quoted as 90.0%; the printed coefficients give 90.4%,
  and no values inside their rounding intervals reach 90.0%. The other thirteen
  quoted probabilities reproduce to their printed precision, so the
  transcription is not in doubt; the 0.4-point gap is in the source text.
* **Table 6 scenarios evaluate the age term at zero.** The Results quote
  probabilities "of the same age" -- 54.5% for the reference patient, for
  example -- that reproduce only with the age term omitted. Age is nonetheless
  uncentred in the model, as the mean-probability identity above confirms.
* **Table 4 age band.** The first age band of Table 4 is printed "18 to < 65"; the
  counts and the next band ("45 to < 65") show it is 18 to < 45.
* **A units slip.** The Results quote the Table 6 scenarios at
  "Ctrough,ss of 5 ug*h/mL"; a trough is a concentration, and 5 ug/mL is used.

## Simulation assumptions

* **Independent covariates.** The virtual cohort draws each risk factor
  independently from its published marginal, except that the CD4 and CD8
  assays share their 46 unreported patients. The real covariates are
  correlated -- above all, the treatment-emergent resistance mutation is more
  common at high exposure -- so the cohort reproduces the overall event rates
  only approximately.
* **Prospective, not post-hoc, exposures, and no concomitant medication.** The
  source exposures are empirical-Bayes predictions with the actual dosing
  history and strong CYP3A inhibitor / inducer use.
* **Placeholder residual error.** Every model carries
  `addSd_prob_* <- fixed(0.001)` only so rxode2 has an error model to attach to
  the probability; the source likelihood is Bernoulli and has no residual
  error. The vignette solves the models with `zeroRe()`.
